census_weighted_mix.caveat: The open synthesis made 7,967 cells for the multiplier with all 182 module boundaries kept, against the tape-out flow's 4,487 -- but that 1.77x was the hierarchy, not the library. Counted like for like, on the netlist flattened except the four multiplier blocks, it is 4,989 cells, 1.11x (Q126(e), docs/reports/data/2026-10-26-open-netlist/README.md, census table; 42,758 transistors against 49,755, 0.86x). So this is still the mix of a different netlist of the same RTL, not of the silicon, and it is used as the mix, not as the count -- but the two netlists are much closer in size than this caveat first said.
census_weighted_mix.source: docs/reports/data/2026-10-26-open-netlist/census_flat.json (Q126(e), same day): core-et's txfma_top synthesized onto ASAP7 RVT with Yosys, 16,087 cells flattened.

conventions.E_transition: E_int_per_transition (VDD only) + 1/2 C_load V^2, the task's formula: the energy drawn from the rail per output transition, averaged over a rise and a fall and over the arc's `when` states. Over a full cycle the load costs C_load V^2 in all.
conventions.drawing_scale: ASAP7's layout is drawn at 4x: every length in the GDS, the LEF and the QRC techfile is four times the real dimension (the kit is drawn on a relaxed 1 nm grid so commercial tools can hold it). THE LIBERTY IS NOT SCALED: the capacitances, energies, delays and leakages here are real-world 7 nm values and need no 4x correction. Only lengths and anything derived from the LEF or QRC do.
conventions.internal_energy: THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS THE VDD GROUP ALONE. ASAP7 splits each internal_power event between VDD and VSS with a negative cross term (INVx1's output rise is +0.120 fJ on VDD and -0.028 fJ on VSS). Summing the two double-counts the same charge in through VDD and out through VSS; part 2's SPICE run measures the rail directly and lands on the VDD-only reading. Every '..._summed_reference_fJ' key is the other convention, kept only because a reader coming from a power tool will see it. rise/fall is the OUTPUT pin's direction.
conventions.leakage: Leakage is the state-averaged VDD entry at 0.7 V and 25 C, in pW. It is NOT scaled to 0.517 V: leakage falls with voltage through DIBL and the subthreshold slope, not as V^2.
conventions.when_states: An arc's `when` groups are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE side-input states and are AVERAGED over, uniformly -- never summed. FAx1's A->SN carries four of them. Summing inflates a state-conditioned cell by the number of its states (1.5x to 8.7x across the cells here); each arc's `by_state` carries the spread.

scope_differences: E60 is BOARD energy (the 129.9 fJ figure) including the regulator's conversion loss; the minion-rail figure, 96.9 fJ, is the one to set against a cell-level estimate, and even that is the whole rail, not the one unit.
E60 is measured 'the cascade included', while this estimate and Q124 cover the Booth rows, the Wallace tree and the product adder only.
E60 is silicon and therefore contains glitches; this estimate and Q124 are zero-delay. tfma.glitch puts the timed tree at 1.4x the energy, so the comparable number is this estimate x 1.4.
e60_measured.source: docs/findings/03-experiments.md, E60 Hamming ladder (aifoundry3, 600 MHz, 0.522 V, h >= 1, 4 passes)
e60_measured.what: E60's measured cost of one flipped mantissa B bit per multiply-add

assumptions: One toggling physical wire = one cell-output transition.

The combinational cell mix is the unweighted mean of a pool of ASAP7 cells -- the gate kinds Q124's census names in the Booth rows, the Wallace tree and the product adder (tfma.asbuilt.cells, tfma.benc, tfma.cmp42). Two pools are carried: the x1 drives and the minimum drives (xp33/xp5) a dense synthesized tree fills up with. The real mix is not in the public data, so the min-to-max spread over each pool is carried too.

Internal energy is the VDD group alone, which part 2's SPICE run confirms is the energy drawn from the rail. The VDD+VSS sum is carried as a labelled reference only -- it double-counts the same charge in through VDD and out through VSS, and is what a power tool reports as 'total internal'.

An arc's mutually exclusive `when` states are AVERAGED, uniformly, never summed. The liberty carries no state probabilities, so a real workload's state statistics would shift the per-cell numbers within the by_state spread each arc carries.

Load per net = pin capacitance of what it drives plus its wire. ASAP7's own input pins are 0.62 fF (INVx1) to about 2 fF (FAx1); wire inside a 30 um tree level at 0.2 fF/um is roughly 0.5-1.5 fF. 1, 2 and 4 fF bracket it; 2 fF is the headline.

Flip-flops: the data-switching (CLK->Q or CLK->QN) arc only. The clock reaches 1,586 of 1,851 flops on every multiply-add either way (tfma.clocked), so the clock-pin energy is not marginal to a flip. The census mix uses the census's own flop, DFFHQx4; the two hand-built pools use the minimum-drive DFFHQNx1. See flop_sensitivity.
Zero-delay, like Q124's count: no glitches. tfma.glitch puts the timed tree at 1.5x the toggles and 1.4x the energy.
Internal energy is scaled from 0.7 V by (0.517/0.7)^2 = 0.5454. That is exact for the capacitive part and optimistic for the short-circuit part, which falls faster than V^2.
ASAP7 is a predictive 7 nm PDK, not TSMC N7, and the ET-SoC-1's cells are not these cells. This is an order-of-magnitude check.

flop_sensitivity.note: 35 of the 381 toggling wires are flop outputs, so the flop choice moves the headline by about 6%, against 2.2x for the per-net load.

headline.central_what: VDD-only internal energy, `when`-state averaged (the convention SPICE confirms in part 2), the cell mix Q126(e) measured for this unit with its own flop DFFHQx4, 2 fF per net, zero delay

compare_like_for_like.what: Q124 is the only like-for-like check: same 381-wire count, same scope (Booth rows, tree, product adder), same zero-delay basis.

implied_net_load_fF.model: E_flip(C) = 60.00 fJ + 50.92 fJ/fF x C, at 0.517 V, census mix, VDD only, zero delay
implied_net_load_fF.note: Q124's band corresponds to a per-net load of about 1.0 to 1.4 fF, which is squarely in the plausible range for a tree-level wire plus a pin. E60's rail figure needs a lighter load still, and once the 1.4x glitch factor is carried it needs a load below any real wire -- but E60 measures a different scope (the cascade included, the whole rail, silicon not zero-delay), so that is a scope gap, not a contradiction.

flow_m_flip_estimate.method:
Price Q124's 381-wire flow-M flip from ASAP7 alone.

    Q124 counted 381 physical wires toggling for 'b bit 11, a = pi' in a
    gate-level, zero-delay run of lane 0: 129 in f1 (19 of them flip-flop
    outputs) and 252 in f2 (16 of them the product register's).  Here each
    toggling wire is priced as one cell-output transition out of ASAP7's
    liberty, at the minion's 0.517 V.

LVT.note: Delay is 50%-to-50%; the liberty's slew is 10-90% with slew_derate_from_library = 1. TT, 0.7 V, 25 C. The input slew is iterated until it equals the stage's own output slew, which is what a chain of these cells settles at.

RVT.note: Delay is 50%-to-50%; the liberty's slew is 10-90% with slew_derate_from_library = 1. TT, 0.7 V, 25 C. The input slew is iterated until it equals the stage's own output slew, which is what a chain of these cells settles at.

fo4_by_vt.note: The brief for this request quoted 'about 8.1 ps RVT at 0.7 V' as the kit's FO4. The kit's own liberty does not give that: see the numbers above. The SPICE run in part 2 is checked against these.

kit.name: ASAP7 7.5-track predictive 7 nm PDK and standard cell library

units.energy: fJ -- the liberty's derived power unit is voltage_unit x current_unit x time_unit = 1 V x 1 mA x 1 ps = 1 fJ

tfma.flip.energy.basis: the real cells' energies, interpolated to 0.517 V

tfma.flip.gate.case: b bit 11 flipped, a = pi (the lab's E60 case)

short_circuit_window.verdict: 0.517 V is ABOVE Vtn + |Vtp| for ASAP7 RVT, by 0.187 V on the saturation thresholds and 0.137 V on the linear ones. So the short-circuit path does NOT close at the minion's rail: both devices can conduct during an input edge. The 20 Oct plan's hope that it might vanish at 0.517 V is wrong for these devices. How much energy that costs against edge time is part 2.
